title: Pan not detected
shortDescription: Zone does not see a compatible ferrous pan.
fullDescription:
LG induction cooktops show F1 when no induction-rated cookware is on the active zone, the pan is too small, or it is offset. The zone pauses until a valid pan is placed.

Glass, copper, and aluminum without an induction layer never work.

fixSteps.title: Magnet test
fixSteps.instruction: Stick a magnet to the pan base. Strong attraction means it works.

fixSteps.title: Use larger pan
fixSteps.instruction: Match pan diameter to the engraved zone size, at least 12 cm for small zones.

fixSteps.title: Center pan
fixSteps.instruction: Slide the pan to the center of the zone.

whenToCallPro: No service unless F1 persists with verified induction cookware.

title: Cooktop overheated
shortDescription: Surface or coil exceeded its thermal limit.
fullDescription: F2 indicates a thermistor reported an unsafe temperature. Empty pans, blocked vents, or a slow cooling fan are common causes. The zone disables until temperature normalizes.

fixSteps.title: Cool down
fixSteps.instruction: Remove pans and let glass cool for 20 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Clear vents
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm cabinet vents below the cooktop are unobstructed.

fixSteps.title: Inspect fan
fixSteps.instruction: If the fault returns, a tech should test the cooling fan and thermistors.

whenToCallPro: Call if F2 returns after the unit cools and vents are clear.

faq.a: Yes, only the affected zone locks out.

title: Touch communication error
shortDescription: User-interface board lost link to main board.
fullDescription: F3 indicates the touch panel and control board are not communicating. Loose ribbons, moisture, or a failed UI board are typical causes. The cooktop disables all zones until the link returns.

fixSteps.title: Reseat ribbon
fixSteps.instruction: From below, reseat the ribbon between UI and main boards.

fixSteps.title: Replace board
fixSteps.instruction: If reseating fails, replace the UI board.

whenToCallPro: Most owners should not pull the cooktop themselves.

faq.q: Could a software update fix this?
faq.a: These cooktops do not get OTA firmware updates.

title: Cooling fan failure
shortDescription: Cooling fan tach signal missing or out of range.
fullDescription: F4 indicates the fan does not report the expected speed. A blocked impeller, dust, a loose connector, or a worn motor causes the fault. Power is cut to protect the inverter.

fixSteps.title: Vacuum vents
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum the intake and exhaust grilles from below.

fixSteps.title: Reseat plug
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect and reconnect the fan tach plug.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: If the fan does not spin freely, replace it.

whenToCallPro: Call if you cannot access the fan from below safely.

faq.q: Can I run with a noisy fan?
faq.a: Briefly, but plan replacement; overheating damages the inverter.

title: IGBT temperature sensor open
fullDescription:
F5 indicates the inverter's temperature sensor is reporting an out-of-range value, almost always a broken connection or failed thermistor.

The cooktop disables the affected zone for safety.

fixSteps.title: Reseat sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat the IGBT thermistor connector and inspect harness for chafe.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: If the sensor reads open at room temperature, replace it.

whenToCallPro: Most homeowners should leave inverter work to a technician.

title: Surface thermistor short
shortDescription: Glass thermistor reports a shorted reading.
fullDescription: F6 means the surface temperature sensor below the glass shows an impossibly high reading. A pinched harness or failed thermistor are typical causes.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Look for pinched or melted insulation near the coil.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the surface thermistor for the affected zone.

whenToCallPro: Call a tech if you cannot lift the cooktop safely.

faq.q: Will a stuck-on burner damage the glass?
faq.a: Possibly; do not use the affected zone until repaired.

title: Inverter over-current
shortDescription: IGBT detected current above safe threshold.
fullDescription: F7 protects the inverter when load current spikes, often from a damaged pan, shorted coil, or failing power semiconductor. The zone is disabled.

fixSteps.title: Try another pan
fixSteps.instruction: Use a known good pan to rule out cookware faults.

fixSteps.title: Inspect coil
fixSteps.instruction: From below, look for soot, cracked ferrites, or burn marks on the coil.

fixSteps.title: Replace inverter
fixSteps.instruction: Damaged IGBT modules require replacing the inverter board.

whenToCallPro: F7 is best handled by a qualified appliance tech.

faq.a: Each zone has its own inverter, so other zones may still work.

title: Mains under-voltage
shortDescription: Supply voltage dropped below operating range.
fullDescription: F9 indicates the cooktop input dropped below approximately 180 V. Brownouts, weak utility supply, or loose breaker terminals are typical causes.

fixSteps.title: Wait and retry
fixSteps.instruction: If the utility is brownout-prone, wait 5 minutes and retry.

fixSteps.title: Measure
fixSteps.instruction: Have an electrician measure L1-L2 at the terminal block; expect 220-244 V.

fixSteps.title: Repair supply
fixSteps.instruction: Address loose connections or panel issues.

whenToCallPro: Always call a licensed electrician for panel work.

faq.a: No, induction cooktops draw too much current for any practical UPS.

title: Power relay fault
shortDescription: Main power relay did not switch correctly.
fullDescription: FP indicates the main mains relay either welded closed or failed to close on command. The cooktop disables all zones for safety. A power-cycle may temporarily clear it but the relay should be replaced.

fixSteps.title: Replace board
fixSteps.instruction: If FP returns, replace the main relay board.

whenToCallPro: FP usually requires a service call.

faq.a: Disconnect it at the breaker until repaired.

title: Child lock active
fullDescription: LOC indicates the child lock is on. To unlock, hold the lock key for 3-5 seconds. If the lock will not clear, the touch panel may be wet or have a stuck key.

fixSteps.title: Hold lock key
fixSteps.instruction: Hold the lock symbol for 3-5 seconds until the chime sounds.

fixSteps.title: Dry the glass
fixSteps.instruction: If unlock fails, dry the entire glass and try again.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: If still locked, flip the breaker for 5 minutes.

whenToCallPro: Service rarely needed unless lock is stuck after a power cycle.

faq.q: Can I disable the lock permanently?
faq.a: No, but it only activates by holding the key.
